# Chapter Thirteen: The Baron's Trap

> *"A predator never hunts in the open when he can wait for the prey to exhaust itself."*

*The Starlight Drifter* shuddered and ground to a complete halt, its engines screaming in futile protest against the crushing power of the dreadnought’s tractor beam.

On the main holo-screen, the transmission channel forced itself open with an authoritative chime.

Resolving in the center of the bridge was the towering, holographic image of Baron Marcus Vargas. The syndicate warlord was clad in polished obsidian armor adorned with gold filigree, his chest and neck heavily reinforced with high-grade cybernetic augments. His cruel, aristocratic face wore an arrogant, predatory smile.

“Captain Campbell,” Vargas’s voice was cultured, smooth, and chillingly devoid of empathy. “I must commend your heroism. Truly inspiring. You sacrificed your ship’s jump reserves to save a handful of worthless asteroid miners.”

“Vargas,” Gracie spat, glaring into the holo-projector. “Turn off the tractor beam, or I’ll ram this ship down your throat.”

Vargas laughed, a dry, mocking sound. 

“With what drive coils, my dear? Your ship is broken. And your prize belongs to me.” Vargas leaned closer to the scanner. “Did you really think your secret was safe? My syndicate purchased the research notes from Vengeance’s black sites. I know all about the little obsidian box nestled in your pretty neck.”

Gracie felt the blood drain from her face.

*He knows...* the passenger whimpered, pure, unadulterated terror flooding back into Gracie's veins. *He wants to cut us open! He’s going to extract the canister! He has the neural scalpels! BLOW THE REACTOR! GRACIE, OVERLOAD THE FUSION CORES! KILL US NOW!*

“Silence!” Gracie hissed aloud, fighting the blinding wave of panic.

Vargas raised an eyebrow, amused. “Ah, I see the passenger is speaking to you. Fascinating. A century of decrypted precursor ciphers and military secrets locked inside a single skull... paired with the Aegis Core’s infinite power. With those two treasures, the Black Sun will rule the entire Orion sector. Even your legendary father won't be able to stop me.”

Vargas’s smile vanished, replaced by cold steel.

“You have two minutes to lower your airlock and surrender the core and yourself. Refuse, and my tractor beam will compress your hull until your lungs collapse in the vacuum.”

The transmission snapped shut.

Silence descended upon the bridge. The hull groaned ominously as the tractor beam tightened its grip, metal buckling along the outer cargo bay.

*Blow the ship...* the Box pleaded, weeping with fear. *Please... don't let them put us on the table again... please...*

Gracie looked at Kael. She looked at Tess. She looked at Unit-7.

“We’re not blowing the ship,” Gracie said, her voice dropping to a deadly, resolute whisper. “And we sure as hell aren't surrendering.”

Kael grinned, his hydraulic titanium fingers flexing with a sharp hiss. “I was hoping you’d say that, Boss. What’s the play?”

“We’re going to give him exactly what he asked for,” Gracie said, her eyes flashing with dangerous fire. “We’re delivering the core in person.”
